title: Mistral releases open weights for its 1-trillion-parameter Large 4 model
subtitle: The mixture-of-experts model activates roughly 52 billion parameters per task and ships under a modified MIT-style Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight license.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: On October 29, Mistral published the weights for Mistral Large 4 — nicknamed Le Chonk — on Hugging Face as Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B. The model is multimodal, uses a mixture-of-experts architecture at roughly one trillion total parameters with about 52 billion active per task, and is covered by what Mistral calls its Ecosystem Open-Weight license, a modified MIT-style license whose terms are worth reading before any production use.

Mistral says the public open-weights release follows about three additional weeks of reinforcement learning after the preview that landed earlier in October. On Terminal-Bench 4.0 — a long-horizon agent benchmark — the score rose from 28% to 41%, which is a meaningful jump for the same base model. A quantised version runs on four NVIDIA B200 or B300 GPUs. The model is also live on Mistral's own API and on Microsoft Foundry.

The release matters because the open-weights frontier has thinned out this year. Meta's Muse Spark landed as 816B open weights earlier in October, Alibaba's Qwen series continues to ship under permissive terms, and a trillion-parameter European release — on a modified MIT-style license, deployable on common inference stacks — gives self-hosting teams a credible alternative to the US-closed-weight ladder. The license modification is the catch: 'open weights' here is not identical to standard MIT, and the Ecosystem terms carry restrictions worth checking.

A note for learners: when you see 'open weights,' read the license. Over the last twelve months, labs have shipped more capable models under more customised licenses — a trend that is reshaping what 'open source AI' actually means in practice. If you work with these models, the hour you spend reading the license is the hour that keeps you out of trouble later. Terms like field-of-use restrictions, downstream distribution, and acceptable-use clauses are not boilerplate.
